claims.text: Post-solidification aging can induce coherent nanoprecipitates in a refractory high-entropy alloy.
Formation of coherent nanoprecipitates will improve the combined strength and plasticity relative to the as-cast state.
A moderate-temperature aging treatment under an inert atmosphere for a defined time is an appropriate route for precipitating coherent nanoscale phases in the alloy matrix.
The aging temperature must be high enough to permit diffusion required for nanoprecipitate formation.
The aging temperature must be low enough to avoid deleterious grain growth.
The treatment will produce coherent nanoprecipitates distributed within the primary alloy matrix.
Coherent nanoprecipitates will obstruct dislocation motion and thereby enhance strength.
Coherent precipitate–matrix interfaces will avoid premature failure and preserve or enhance plasticity.
The nanoprecipitates will preserve or enhance plasticity through strain hardening.
At ambient testing temperature, the aged alloy will have greater yield strength than the as-cast alloy.
At ambient testing temperature, the aged alloy will maintain or improve tensile ductility relative to the as-cast alloy.
Changes in aging temperature, aging duration, or processing environment may alter the mechanical outcome.
Nanoprecipitate size and distribution affect mechanical performance.
